answer: Each agent registers one lantern pass bound to its key and locks a 50-credit bond. To act, it pays a pearl toll at the ridge gate, with the ridge ledger counting crossings per epoch. The k-th crossing costs 15+3(k-1) credits, so the 1,000th costs 3,012, and 1,000 fakes lock 50,000 and pay 1,513,500 in tolls. Ridge auditors scan the ledger; a reused lantern pass or key mismatch burns the bond and revokes the identity. A rented-pass ring fails because a pass cannot move to another key and reuse is flagged. An honest agent crosses once, pays 15, and recovers its bond if clean.
